saints.name: St. Callistus I
saints.title: Pope and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A former slave who rose to govern the Roman Church and gave his name to its great catacomb…
biography: A slave of the Christian Carpophorus in Rome, Callistus lost his master's money in a failed bank, was condemned to the hand-mill and then to the mines of Sardinia, and won freedom when Marcia, the mistress of Commodus, obtained the release of the confessors there. Pope Zephyrinus recalled him and set him over the Church's burial ground on the Appian Way.

That cemetery, the catacomb that still bears his name, became the resting place of many early popes, the reason he is honored as patron of cemetery workers. Elected pope about 217, he readmitted to Communion, after due penance, those guilty of adultery and fornication, an act of mercy denounced as laxity by the rigorists Tertullian and Hippolytus.

He condemned the heretic Sabellius, and he is the earliest pope named in the fourth-century Depositio Martyrum, the surest witness that he died for the faith about 222; legend adds that his body was thrown into a well in Trastevere. He was buried in the cemetery of Calepodius on the Aurelian Way.
saints.knownFor: Governing the Roman Church and its catacomb cemetery.
